description: Construction of a two storey side extension, a single storey rear extension, relocation of the entrance to the front and the construction of a hip-to-gable roof extension to accommodate a rear dormer extension including two roof lights to the front to facilitate conversion of roof space into habitable accommodation
decision_conditions:
<div>The proposed development by reason of scale, siting, design, bulk and mass of the proposed development would be an undesirable addition, representing an overly dominant and excessive addition to the semi-detached dwelling. The excessive depth of the rear extension combined with the cumulative impact of the side extension would result in the appearance of overdevelopment of the site. As such, the proposal would cause undue harm to the character and appearance of the host dwelling and surrounding area. As such, the proposed development is contrary to:<br></div><div><br></div><div><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
National Planning Policy Framework </span>National Planning Policy Framework
(NPPF) (MHCLG, 2024)<o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; line-height: 107%; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">- Policy D4 of the
London Plan (March 2021)</span></p><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; line-height: 107%; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">- The Residential
Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)<o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal">









</p><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of </span>The London Borough of Barking and
Dagenham’s Local Plan: (September 2024)<o:p></o:p></p></div>

<div>The proposed single storey rear extension by reason of scale, siting and design&nbsp; would be an undesirable addition which would cause an unacceptable level of overshadowing and overbearing impact to neighbouring dwellings. This would result in a harmful impact to the amenity currently enjoyed by neighbouring occupiers. As such, the proposal fails to protect residential amenity and constitutes un-neighbourly development. It therefore fails to accord with the following policies which seek to ensure that development proposals protect residential amenity:&nbsp;<br></div><div><br></div><div><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
